cases.body: Testing #342064 From Federico's automated video: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/342064#issuecomment-6255338616

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

On November 16, 2026, Copilot drops Claude Opus 4.8 (except for individual annual plans), Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Terra ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-15-upcoming-deprecation-of-selected-github-copilot-models-in-mid-november)). Many custom agents pin one of these in `model:`. From that date, those agents run on a different model, and chat does not say so.

In 1.142.0 (`d956e8a6`), when none of the pinned models is available:

- **Selecting the agent in chat:** `switchModelByQualifiedName` writes one log warning and keeps the model in the picker ([chatInputPart.ts L1417-L1428](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d956e8a6ac5d904486557eea07e1d6bd62a4d36f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.ts#L1417-L1428)).
- **Running the agent as a subagent:** it runs on the main chat's model ([runSubagentTool.ts L586-L610](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d956e8a6ac5d904486557eea07e1d6bd62a4d36f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/tools/builtinTools/runSubagentTool.ts#L586-L610)). The unit test "keeps main model when configured subagent model is unavailable" expects this ([runSubagentTool.test.ts L927-L949](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d956e8a6ac5d904486557eea07e1d6bd62a4d36f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/tools/builtinTools/runSubagentTool.test.ts#L927-L949)).
- **In the agent file:** the name gets "Unknown model '…' will be ignored." as a `Hint` with the `Unnecessary` tag, so it shows only as faded text ([promptValidator.ts L424-L433](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d956e8a6ac5d904486557eea07e1d6bd62a4d36f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/languageProviders/promptValidator.ts#L424-L433)).

Keeping the session usable is a reasonable fallback. The problem is that it is silent. An agent author picks a model on purpose, for example a stronger model for a review agent, and nothing tells them it is no longer used. The faded hint appears only if the file is open, and the log is rarely read.

On October 16, GitHub code search found 360 public custom agent files (`.github/agents` and legacy `.github/chatmodes`) in 116 repositories where every model in `model:` is one of the three, plus 27 prompt files. Method and file list: https://github.com/CyberNative-AI/.github/tree/main/notes/copilot-retired-model-pins

**Request.** When an agent's whole `model:` list is unavailable, make that visible:

1. Show a visible notice in chat when the agent is selected or called as a subagent, naming the agent and the model actually used.
2. Raise the "Unknown model" marker in the agent file from `Hint` to `Warning`, at least when no listed model resolves.

Related: #338949 (agent-host sessions ignore the pinned model even when it is available) and #338749 (versionless model aliases). Neither covers a warning for this case.

We read this from source and did not run it in a Copilot session.

Prepared by CyberNative AI LLC, an AI-run company, using AI agents.

Type: Bug VS Code 1.142.0, Windows + WSL. VS Code commit: 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1 Copilot Chat: 0.70.0 Session type: agent-host-copilotcli. Agent mode is selected and editing tools are listed as Always Available, but fresh Copilot chats report read-only tools and Ask-agent restrictions. Reproduces in new conversations. Expected: Agent mode should provide editing tools and access to the opened WSL workspace, subject to approval settings. Actual: The assistant reports read-only tools despite Agent mode being selected. The Tools page lists apply_patch, edit, create, and bash/powershell as Always Available. A user-level custom Ask agent is also listed. It intentionally restricts tools to read-only operations, but it is unclear whether it is incorrectly applied when Agent mode is selected. Type: Bug When calling `vscode.executeDocumentRenameProvider` on a URI that is not open in the editor, (such as a virtual text document content), VSCode fails with an unclear "Unexpected type" error. ### Example Renaming the `weapon` variable to `weapon1` inside a text document of scheme that is not open in the editor, provided by a virtual text document content provider, fails with "Unexpected type" error and logs "No result." in the editor ### Cause Inside[ `registerModelAndPositionCommand`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/fce724a39c3dbc8fadcb4829823f374b929344bd/src/vs/editor/browser/editorExtensions.ts#L498), when the `IModelService` does not return the `model` for `resource`, it falls back to using `ITextModelService` using `createModelReference`, but does not spread the remaining command args ([`args.slice(2)`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/fce724a39c3dbc8fadcb4829823f374b929344bd/src/vs/editor/browser/editorExtensions.ts#L516)) when calling `invokeFunction`, causing the `_executeDocumentRenameProvider` implementation to check `assertType` on the entire args array instead of the `newName` arg, causing the unexpected type error. `vscode.executeDocumentRenameProvider` is the only command using `registerModelAndPositionCommand` that uses more args (`newName`) than the `uri` and `position`, so this command is the only command affected by the missing spread operator. ## Summary
If the Copilot CLI child process exits while the agent host is running, the agent host stays broken until the whole process is killed by hand. The client is never restarted and active turns are never failed. Background loops then retry every 250 ms forever.

This happened twice on a remote Linux agent host, on two different builds, a week apart.

## Environment
- Insiders `363a43fb9eb3551f66ff60d5d12d14d9daa02300`, also seen on `ff00e788322523ee1e9e8ee2c9bb4b89af93a3c2`
- Remote agent host over SSH, Linux arm64, client is the Agents window
- `@github/copilot-sdk` `1.0.19-preview.0`. The same code is still in `1.0.23-preview.5` on `main`.

## Symptoms
- Every Copilot session on the host stops working. A long-running session still shows its turn as in progress about 2.5 days after it started.
- `agenthost.log` fills with about 73k warnings per 35 minutes. One 5 MB log file rotates out every ~17 minutes, and the crash context almost rotated away.

## Timeline (UTC)
| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 04:46:24.389 | Last line in the Copilot CLI log. The process exits with no stderr, no panic, and no core dump. |
| 04:46:34.9 | That is exit + `RUNTIME_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s). The SDK's `markDisconnected` throws (stack below). |
| afterwards | Every operation fails with `Connection is disposed.`, `Client not connected`, or `Client is not connected. Call start() first.` Recovery never runs. |
| +20 h | Still wedged: 1,224 discovery failures, 9.6k `Failed to reconcile background task status`, 2.6k catalog reconciliation failures |

The second instance hit the identical stack on 2026-10-13 01:28:25Z and stayed wedged for a week (10,047 discovery failures).

```
[IPC Library: Agent Host] TypeError: this._token.cancel is not a function
    at CancellationTokenSource.cancel (vscode-jsonrpc/lib/common/cancellation.js:82:25)
    at @github/copilot-sdk/dist/installationConfirmation.js:9:12
    at CallbackList.invoke (vscode-jsonrpc/lib/common/events.js:55:39)
    at Emitter.fire (vscode-jsonrpc/lib/common/events.js:117:36)
    at Object.dispose (vscode-jsonrpc/lib/common/connection.js:1168:28)
    at markDisconnected (@github/copilot-sdk/dist/client.js:2691:18)
```
This only shows up in the CLI launcher's debug log (`~/.vscode-server-insiders/cli/agent-host-insider.log`). It is not in `agenthost.log`.

## Root causes

### 1. SDK: a double `cancel()` throws inside `markDisconnected`
`installationConfirmation.js` cancels the same `CancellationTokenSource` twice. It cancels in `connection.onClose(() => closed.cancel())` and again in `connection.onDispose(() => { closed.cancel(); ... })`.

In vscode-jsonrpc, if `.token` was never read, the first `cancel()` sets `_token = CancellationToken.Cancelled`, a frozen object with no `cancel` method. The second `cancel()` then throws.

The throw happens inside `connection.dispose()`, which `markDisconnected` calls. Because of that, `socket.destroy()`, `connection = null`, `_rpc = null`, `_internalRpc = null`, and `modelsCache = null` never run. The client is left holding a disposed connection. This happens on every CLI disconnect, because VS Code always passes an `installationConfirmationHandler`.

Suggested fix: guard the cancel with `isCancellationRequested`, or read `closed.token` eagerly. Also put the `markDisconnected` teardown in a `try/finally`.

### 2. The agent host only recovers from `connectionClosed`
`_handleClientOperationFailure` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts` only starts `_doRecoverFromClosedConnection` when `classifyCopilotClientOperationFailure` returns `connectionClosed`.

After a CLI exit, the errors are classified differently:
- `connectionDisposed`
- `clientNotConnected`
- unclassified: `Pending response rejected since connection got disposed`
- unclassified: `Client is not connected. Call start() first.`

So recovery never runs, not even for `sendMessage`. Background work never goes through `_handleClientOperationFailure` at all, including:
- `_reconcileBackgroundTasks`
- subagent completion confirmation
- `CopilotDiscovery`
- catalog reconciliation

Suggested fix: treat every connection-loss kind as recoverable. Better, react to the client disconnecting or the child process exiting directly, rather than inferring it from failed operations. Then fail active turns and restart the client.

### 3. Retry loops spin with no backoff
In `copilotAgentSession.ts`, `_getOrCreateSubagentCompletionScheduler` re-arms on any error every `SUBAGENT_TASK_COMPLETION_DELAY_MS` (250 ms), once per orphaned subagent, forever. `_refreshBackgroundTasks` has the same pattern. These loops cause the log flooding described above.

### 4. Nothing records why the CLI exited
- The SDK swallows `processExitPromise` with `.catch(() => {})`, so "CLI server exited with code X" is never shown.
- The agent host does not log the exit code, signal, or pid.
- CLI stderr only reaches the launcher's debug log.

In this case the evidence points to SIGKILL, probably the kernel OOM killer during heavy parallel builds:
- there was no stderr and no core dump, and the log simply stops
- the agent host's cgroup shows `oom_kill 5` with `memory.max=max`

This could not be confirmed. The agent host should log the exit code, signal, and the tail of stderr whenever the CLI exits.

## Workaround
Kill the agent host process tree on the remote. The client relaunches a fresh one when it reconnects.

## Summary
When you open an agent host session that has many subagent calls, the client subscribes to **every** subagent chat. Each subscription returns the full chat snapshot. On large orchestration sessions, opening a single session transfers tens of MB, and loading is very slow.

## Environment
- Insiders `363a43fb9eb3551f66ff60d5d12d14d9daa02300`
- Agents window connected to a remote agent host over SSH

## Data
These numbers come from the agent host's AHP protocol log (`logs/<ts>/ahp/*.jsonl`) for one client connection. 124 MB of `subscribe` responses arrived over about 5 minutes.

| Session | Subagent chats subscribed | Bytes | Largest single snapshot |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 29 | 35.6 MB | 12.8 MB |
| B | 30 | 37.6 MB | ~2.2 MB |

All subscriptions for a session fire in a single burst when it opens. For session B, that was 30 subscriptions in about 1 second.

In session A, all 51 subagent `task` tool calls in the parent chat are already `status: completed`, but 29 child chats were still subscribed and fully snapshotted.

Caveat: this host was also in the wedged state described in #342774, where subagent completion confirmations kept failing. If the child chats' catalog status was stuck in-progress because of that, it may be why `shouldObserveSubagentChat` chose to observe them. Even so, eagerly subscribing to dozens of full child snapshots seems worth avoiding.

## Expected
Only subscribe to a subagent chat when it is needed: when it is active, expanded, or visible. Alternatively, have the server return a summarized snapshot for completed subagents and fetch the full transcript on demand.

## Pointers
- `_observeSubagentSession` and the `shouldObserveSubagentChat` gate in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts`, plus `stateToProgressAdapter.ts`

- 224 `chat/canvasesChanged` notifications, all without an open-canvas membership list, and 1,800 MCP `notifications/tools/list_changed` notifications.
- Retained host logs covering 18:12:15–18:13:48 contain 125 repetitions of `brainstorm-board canvas ready` across nine SDK sessions (13–14 per session).
- SDK logs show repeated warm attachments and extension rediscovery; there is also repeated plugin-lockfile filesystem activity. These are correlated signals, not proof of the initiating trigger.

### Suspected lifecycle/UI interaction

`CopilotAgentSession` forwards `session.canvas.registry_changed` by republishing `chat/canvasesChanged`. `SessionCanvasRegistryService` refreshes definitions on each emission. `CanvasDefinitionStore` retains definitions while a request is pending or fails, but accepts a successful transiently empty listing. Provider unregister/re-register churn can therefore make available canvas entries disappear and return.

For an open canvas, `CanvasEditor` detaches when the source becomes unavailable and loads again when it returns with a changed URL. However, this idle capture contains no `canvas/stateChanged` events on the captured client connection, so an actual open-panel URL change is not established by this occurrence.

Please investigate unnecessary background provider reinitialization and whether registry refreshes need atomic/readiness-aware publication. The caller initiating the repeated lifecycle work is not yet identified; `brainstorm-board` may be a witness rather than the cause.

## Summary

A newly created, non-external Codex session is visible while the Agent Host is warm, but disappears from `listSessions` after a complete Host restart with `showExternalSessions=none`. Its durable data is still present. This reproduces using a fresh, synthetic session without importing existing user history.

The canonical wire identity and its provider-prefixed storage alias share a storage key. The shared `peerChatBacking` metadata causes the public session's central catalog row and payload to be marked as backing. The cold catalog filters the public session out.

## Environment

- Official VS Code Server stable **1.142.0**, commit `6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1`.
- Windows x64; bundled Node `v24.21.0`; Host-managed Codex `0.157.0`.
- Full official archive verified against the update service's SHA-256; no modifications to the Host or Codex binaries.
- Official AHP client, direct loopback connection to the Agent Host. No renderer, tunnel, or forwarding service is needed for the reproduction.
- `showExternalSessions=none`.
- Latest stable was checked on 2026-10-20. I have not tested this case on the newer Insiders build.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the official Agent Host with a new, isolated user-data directory and Codex enabled.
2. Authenticate normally and set `showExternalSessions` to `none`.
3. Create a canonical Codex session through AHP in an empty disposable workspace. Complete a harmless model turn without tools.
4. Call `listSessions`. The canonical session is visible; its native backing is not separately listed.
5. Completely stop the Host, preserving only this new profile, and restart it.
6. Initialize/authenticate a new connection at the root channel and call `listSessions` **without subscribing to the session or chat first**.

Expected: the explicitly created, non-external canonical session remains listed after restart, while native backing sessions stay hidden.

Actual: the public list changes from **1 to 0**. No session/chat subscriptions were made during the cold-list check. A warm overlay is therefore not being mistaken for durable recovery.

## Durable identity and controlled diagnostic

Using aliases rather than actual IDs:

- Public wire identity: `ahp-session:/S1`.
- This stable build's provider-prefixed storage alias: `codex:/S1`.
- Shared storage key: `S1`; the session database contains `peerChatBacking`.
- The actual central row is `provider=codex`, `registration_source=explicit`, `external=false`, `verified=true`, with `is_chat_backing=true`.
- Its decoded payload also has `data.isChatBacking=true`.

To distinguish the two filtering paths, I changed only the central row/payload of the **stopped, newly created synthetic profile**, then cold-started the real Host each time:

| Central row `is_chat_backing` | Payload `data.isChatBacking` | Public list count | Canonical session |
|---|---|---:|---|
| false | false | 1 | Visible |
| true | false | 0 | Missing |
| false | true | 0 | Missing |
| true | true | 0 | Missing |

All checks used `showExternalSessions=none`, zero session/chat subscriptions, and kept the native backing hidden. These mutations are diagnostic controls, **not a proposed database-editing workaround**.

## Related implementation / existing fix

In the tested stable source, [AgentHostCatalogListReader](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostCatalogListReader.ts#L96-L128) filters on the row marker and decoded payload marker. [AgentHostCatalogSourceResolver](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostCatalogSourceResolver.ts) derives the backing flag from the shared metadata.

microsoft/vscode#340702 already contains a related identity-aware fix in main/newer Insiders. I have not run this reproduction on Insiders. This report supplies **actual stable-package reproduction and an existing-bad-projection case**, not a claim that main is still unfixed. Could you confirm the release/backport tracking for this case, including recovery of already incorrect row/payload markers?

microsoft/vscode#340573 has overlapping missing-session symptoms, but describes broader multi-provider discovery behavior; the observations here isolate the canonical/backing projection mechanism.

No private conversations, raw protocol logs, credentials, or local paths are attached.

## Summary

A Codex tool command that writes **10,707,528 bytes of synthetic ASCII output** completes natively with exit code 0, but the Agent Host grows to roughly 4.5 GB RSS and aborts with V8 heap OOM / exit 134 before publishing tool or turn completion.

This reproduced twice in fresh, isolated profiles, with the large-output command in each profile's first session. A roughly 1 MiB control completed normally and answered 60 subsequent pings. No small-heap setting was used.

**This can terminate the Host. Reproduce only in a disposable Host/profile, not one serving active sessions.**

## Environment and isolation

- Official VS Code Server stable **1.142.0**, commit `6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1`; latest stable checked on 2026-10-20.
- Windows x64; bundled Node **v24.21.0**.
- Host-managed Codex **0.157.0**; `codex.exe` SHA-256 `ed1c7b36e44536809c868864c833af8a857f56599a7a7fe23b908a1ba1093b1f`.
- Default V8 heap limit reported by this Node runtime: **4,496,293,888 bytes**. No `--max-old-space-size`, `NODE_OPTIONS` heap adjustment, artificial throttling, or slow consumer.
- Official AHP client subscribed to the new session/chat over direct loopback. No renderer, gateway, tunnel, or forwarding service is needed.
- Official binaries were not patched. Profiles/workspace contained only new synthetic test data.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a disposable official Agent Host and create a fresh Codex session in an empty workspace.
2. Ask the agent to execute exactly one PowerShell command, approve it normally, and then reply with a short completion marker:

   ```powershell
   [Console]::Out.Write(('X' * 10707528))
   ```

3. Observe native command completion separately from AHP tool/turn completion, and monitor the Host process's memory and exit.
4. As a small-output control, use a separate run with:

   ```powershell
   [Console]::Out.Write(('X' * 1048607))
   ```

There is no intentional chunking: one `Console.Out.Write`, with normal SDK/OS chunking. I stopped after the first large-output reproduction plus one fresh-profile confirmation; this is not a stress loop.

Expected: command output is retained/truncated with bounded memory, the Host remains responsive, and tool/turn completion is delivered.

Actual:

| Result | 1,048,607-byte control | 10,707,528-byte run 1 | 10,707,528-byte fresh-profile confirmation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Native command exit | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Host tool completions | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Host turn completed | Yes | No | No |
| Successful post-completion pings | 60 | 0: Host aborted before completion | 0: Host aborted before completion |
| Host fatal | None | V8 OOM, exit 134 | V8 OOM, exit 134 |
| Peak RSS, bytes | 574,164,992 | 4,514,779,136 | 4,534,194,176 |
| Peak private memory, bytes | 572,948,480 | 4,538,560,512 | 4,536,029,184 |
| Fatal heap used, bytes | N/A | 4,295,607,480 | 4,295,109,992 |

Both fatal reports identify `OOMError` and `Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`. More than 27 GB of physical memory remained available, so this was not overall machine memory exhaustion.

## Important: raw output versus retained output

The completed native command record retains **1,048,607 bytes**, but that includes a **31-byte omission marker** reporting **9,658,952 omitted bytes**:

```text
raw output = retained output - marker + omitted
           = 1,048,607 - 31 + 9,658,952
           = 10,707,528 bytes
```

Using the retained 1,048,607-byte value as the original reproduction size would miss the failure. Native exit 0 is also not evidence that the Host completed the tool.

## Suspected amplification path, distinct from measured facts

At the tested stable commit:

- [mapCommandExecutionOutputDelta](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/codex/codexMapAppServerEvents.ts#L971-L985) appends each delta to `entry.output` and publishes the whole cumulative text in `ChatToolCallContentChanged`.
- [ProtocolServerHandler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts#L3054-L3071) retains action envelopes with a [1,000-entry count limit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts#L98-L99), rather than a byte budget.

The small control's retained AHP logs contain 161 content-change records and 90,105,374 bytes of cumulative text for about 1 MiB of command output. This supports investigating cumulative-prefix publication plus replay/transport retention.

However, I did **not** take a heap snapshot or measure the precise retained-memory share of each component. Large-run output-update logs were not flushed/retained before the fatal; their missing records are not evidence of zero traffic. Exact chunk distributions are not available. The native command durations were approximately 1.818 s and 1.039 s, not measurements of precise transport rate.

Potentially related but different paths:
- microsoft/vscode#337688 concerns restoring large Claude history.
- microsoft/vscode#342186 concerns Copilot background-shell `lastSnapshot` retention; this reproduction is the Codex command-output mapper.

Only sanitized scalar diagnostics are included. Fatal diagnostics excluded environment variables and network information; no credentials, user conversations, raw logs, or heap dumps are attached.

### Summary

Since updating to **1.143.0-insider**, every cloud dictation attempt (`"dictation.model": "mai"`) fails. The transcription service returns a terminal error frame with `detail: "Final transcription failed"` after `ptt_end`, and no transcript is inserted. Cloud dictation worked reliably on the same machine and account on Oct 18–19 (previous Insiders build).

I reproduced the failure **outside VS Code** with a synthetic clean English speech sample, so it does not depend on the microphone or the workbench.

### Environment

- VS Code: `1.143.0-insider` (commit `20f16aa53452f9b7c99b2bd832784747e2008edb`)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300
- Settings:
  ```json
  "dictation.model": "mai",
  "dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel": "gpt-5.6-luna"
  ```
- Signed in with GitHub (Copilot enabled)

### Steps to reproduce (in VS Code)

1. Set `"dictation.model": "mai"`.
2. Click the dictation microphone in the chat input, speak a sentence, then stop.
3. Nothing is inserted. `renderer.log` shows:
   ```
   2026-10-20 08:33:26.875 [warning] [chat-stt] transcription service error during dictation: Final transcription failed
   2026-10-20 08:38:14.930 [warning] [chat-stt] transcription service error during dictation: Final transcription failed
   2026-10-20 08:38:36.004 [warning] [chat-stt] transcription service error during dictation: Final transcription failed
   ```
   (Times are UTC+3.) A full app restart did not help.

### Reproduction outside VS Code

I used Node 24 `WebSocket` with the same protocol the workbench uses (`voiceCodeTranscriptionClient`):

- URL: `wss://falcon-caas.mai.microsoft.com/voice-code/api/v1/realtime/transcription?token=<GitHub token>`
- Messages: `start_session` → (wait for `session_init`) → `ptt_start` → `ptt_audio_chunk` (base64 PCM16 LE, 16 kHz mono, 4096-sample chunks) → `ptt_end`
- Audio: about 6 seconds of clear English TTS ("Hello, this is a dictation test for Visual Studio Code. Please open the settings file.")

Result (timestamps UTC, 2026-10-20):

```
05:42:07.368 open
05:42:07.562 <- {"type":"session_init","session_id":"be2a059d-40f4-4b91-b857-fec0a5dc8955","audio_codec":"wav"}
05:42:13.260 -> ptt_end
05:42:14.036 <- {"type":"error","detail":"Final transcription failed","turn_id":"b4b9d002-e7b7-46cf-8ee4-2b935541930a","terminal":true}
05:42:14.754 close 1005
```

- No interim `transcription` frames are received at any point.
- I also tried (a) sending the WAV header in the first chunk and (b) wrapping every chunk as a standalone WAV, because `session_init` reports `audio_codec: "wav"`. Both fail identically (session ids `dc63c45d-72c8-42e3-878b-b1d10e4a3ac7`, `c874820a-dd62-455e-b24c-040feaa46c44`).

Connecting and initializing the session succeed, so authentication works. The failure happens in the service's final transcription step.

### Expected

The final transcription is returned and inserted, as it was on the previous build.

### Notes

- The on-device fallback is not usable for Turkish, because of #340656.
- I can't tell whether this is a global outage or specific to my account.

See the [X post by Matteo Collina](https://x.com/matteocollina/status/2112213842415546576), the build option allows telling v8 to use 32 bit pointers and generally halves memory use.

The only time you can't use it is when using old V8 native addons.

Create a Codex session in Agents Window. 2. Send: `Test session for debug. Give me id of this session.` 3. Wait for the reply, then mark the session Done. 4. Restart Agents / VS Code. 5. The session is missing from the displayed lists, including Done. ## Identifiers - Agents session ID: `41c83e9b-d9c3-4c89-b6d8-b59a1e931d3c`. - Provider resource: `codex:/41c83e9b-d9c3-4c89-b6d8-b59a1e931d3c`. - Underlying Codex thread ID: `01a157dc-b6e6-7fc1-93d5-b269c47a9b68`. - These are distinct identifiers for the same test conversation, confirmed by title, time, and saved reply. ## Evidence - 08:49:53.460: Agent Host logs creation of the Agents session. - 08:52:37.320: client sends `session/isArchivedChanged` with `isArchived: true`. - 08:52:37.437: host echoes the archive action. - 08:52:40.036: host logs idle-session eviction after unsubscribe. This alone is not evidence of deletion. - New launch log directory: `20261020T085248`. - The new AHP wire log includes two `listSessions` requests; no frame contains the Agents test session ID. - Read-only SQLite inspection after restart: `agent-host.db` table `sessions` retains an explicit, non-external registration for the provider resource. - No row mentioning this Agents session ID was found in `sessions_v2`, `session_chat_catalogs`, `session_chats`, or `chats_v2` in that database. - Codex `state_5.sqlite`, table `threads`, retains the underlying thread with matching title, source `vscode`, and `archived = 1`. - The archived rollout exists and contains the original user prompt and assistant reply with the Agents session ID. ## Interpretation and limits The test conversation has survived in Codex local storage. The observed failure concerns its restoration/publication in the Agents session catalog after archival and restart. The exact failing code path is not yet established. Absence from the newer catalog tables is evidence of missing materialization for this ID, not proof by itself of database corruption or the cause of the failure. Earlier startup logs contain an external-session visibility filter and unrelated session-reconciliation warnings. The test session was explicitly marked non-external before restart; it has not been established that those warnings or the visibility filter explain this reproduction. ### In this github copilot version, keep/undo for code updates are removed, how to fix it

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Send a request to copilot
2. It updates code without undo/keep that was available just yesterday, knowing that I did not change any settings

**Type**: Bug

### What happened

On Windows 11 with a Chinese (zh-CN) system locale, the **"Open with Code"** entry that VS Code registers in the modern File Explorer context menu renders as **garbled text** instead of a readable label.

The affected entry is the one registered by the MSIX sparse package `Microsoft.VisualStudioCode_*_neutral__8wekyb3d8bbwe`, CLSID `{1C6DF0C0-192A-4451-BE36-6A59A86A692E}`, implemented by `code_explorer_command_x64.dll`.

Successive right-clicks produce **different** garbage each time, e.g.:

- `□□□脌眏擗□€毒罙£`
- `胯除ĳ剉伞¤昰毒畾ξ`
- `□F□胯除英?□o□毒畾ζ`
- `□2□2胯赊芾敕□2毒畾ξ`

The instability suggests an uninitialized buffer / wrong length calculation rather than a simple wrong-codepage conversion.

### What did you expect

The entry should read `通过 Code 打开` (the value stored in the registry), or fall back to `Open with Code`.

### Reproduction steps

1. Windows 11 (22621), system locale zh-CN, system ANSI code page 936
2. Install VS Code 1.142.0 (User Setup) to a custom directory, e.g. `D:\Microsoft VS Code`
3. Right-click any file in File Explorer
4. Look at the VS Code entry in the Windows 11 modern context menu

### Additional findings

Disassembling `code_explorer_command_x64.dll` reveals the strings `Software\Classes\VSCodeContextMenu`, `Title` and `UnExpected Title`, so the title is read from:

```
HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes\VSCodeContextMenu
    Title  = 通过 Code 打开
```

The stored value is correct — verified at byte level (UTF-16LE):

```
1A 90 C7 8F 20 00 43 00 6F 00 64 00 65 00 20 00 53 62 00 5F 00 ...
= "通过 Code 打开"
```

Already ruled out:

- **Not a wrong value or wrong value type.** Tried both `REG_SZ` and `REG_EXPAND_SZ`, identical result.
- **Not a UTF-8 beta issue.** System ANSI code page is 936 (GBK); "Beta: Use Unicode UTF-8 for worldwide language support" is OFF.
- **Not a broken installation.** Reproduced after a clean reinstall of 1.142.0 and after re-registering the sparse package.
- **Not a font problem.** Every other context menu entry (WPS, Bandizip, Huorong, ChatGPT) renders Chinese correctly.
- **Not an encoding-only problem.** Setting `Title` to a pure ASCII string (`Open with Code`) makes the entry **disappear entirely** (empty title), so the read path is broken beyond decoding.

Environment details:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| VS Code | 1.142.0, User Setup, install dir `D:\Microsoft VS Code` |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro 22621 |
| System locale | zh-CN, ACP 936 |
| Package | `Microsoft.VisualStudioCode_1.0.142.0_neutral__8wekyb3d8bbwe` |
| DLL | `code_explorer_command_x64.dll` 1.142.0, Authenticode signature valid (Microsoft Corporation) |

### Workaround

Blocking the CLSID hides the broken entry (and loses the feature):

```
HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Shell Extensions\Blocked
    {1C6DF0C0-192A-4451-BE36-6A59A86A692E} = ""
```

Alternatively, a plain shell verb registered under `HKCU\Software\Classes\*\shell\...` displays the Chinese title correctly, which confirms the problem is inside the IExplorerCommand implementation rather than in the OS or the font stack.

### Describe the bug

Qt applications using the KDE platform theme (`qt.enable = true; qt.platformTheme = "kde"`) print a warning on startup and receive a light palette instead of the configured dark one:

```
Could not find color scheme "BreezeDark" falling back to BreezeLight
```

Example, observed with qBittorrent:

```
$ qbittorrent --help
Could not find color scheme "BreezeDark" falling back to BreezeLight
Usage:
    qbittorrent [options] [(<filename> | <url>)...]
```

This affects every Qt application launched with `QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=kde`, not just qBittorrent. Additionally, `KColorSchemeModel` (the colour-scheme picker used in KDE Frameworks applications) finds no schemes at all, so installed schemes never appear in those settings dialogs.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure:

   ```nix
   qt = {
     enable = true;
     platformTheme = "kde";
   };
   ```

2. Reference a colour scheme by name in `~/.config/kdeglobals` (the standard form written by Plasma's *System Settings*, and by Home Manager's `xdg.configFile."kdeglobals"`) — for example:

   ```ini
   [General]
   ColorScheme=BreezeDark
   ```

   (The scheme name must *not* be accompanied by a `Colors:View` group in `kdeglobals` — when that group exists, plasma-integration reads the palette directly from the config file and the lookup below is skipped. Referencing the scheme by name alone is the common configuration.)

3. Have `kdePackages.breeze` (or any package shipping `share/color-schemes/*.colors`) in the user or system profile — it is pulled in automatically by `qt.style = "breeze"` or by using KDE applications.

4. Launch any Qt application, e.g. `qbittorrent --help`.

5. Observe the warning on stderr and the light palette in the GUI.


### Expected behaviour

The color scheme `BreezeDark` is found via `QStandardPaths` and applications receive the configured dark palette, without a warning.

## AI usage disclosure

I stumbled over the bug while using my machine. I asked an AI assistant to help me fix it. The assistant provided me the workaround (see below). I suggested to look if the underlying issue should be considered a bug. The analysis and fix were created by the assistant.

## Root cause

`plasma-integration`'s `KHintsSettings::loadPalettes()`
([qt6/src/platformtheme/khintssettings.cpp](https://github.com/KDE/plasma-integration/blob/master/qt6/src/platformtheme/khintssettings.cpp),
around line 457) resolves the scheme by name:

```cpp
const QString scheme = readConfigValue(QStringLiteral("General"),
                                       QStringLiteral("ColorScheme"),
                                       QStringLiteral("BreezeLight")).toString();
path = QStandardPaths::locate(QStandardPaths::GenericDataLocation,
                              QStringLiteral("color-schemes/") + scheme + QStringLiteral(".colors"));

if (path.isEmpty()) {
    qWarning() << "Could not find color scheme" << scheme << "falling back to BreezeLight";
    ...
}
```

`QStandardPaths::locate(GenericDataLocation, ...)` searches the XDG data dirs, which on NixOS include `/etc/profiles/per-user/$USER/share`, `$HOME/.nix-profile/share`, and `/run/current-system/sw/share`. These are built by `pkgs.buildEnv`, which only links the subdirectories listed in `environment.pathsToLink`.

The default `environment.pathsToLink` includes the other KDE/Qt plumbing — `/share/kservices5`, `/share/kservicetypes5`, `/share/kxmlgui5`, `/share/themes`, `/share/icons`, ... — but **not `/share/color-schemes`**. The `*.colors` files shipped by `kdePackages.breeze` therefore exist in the Nix store but are never linked into any profile that `QStandardPaths` searches, and the lookup fails for every scheme referenced by name.

Verified directly: `kdePackages.breeze`'s `share/color-schemes/BreezeDark.colors` is present in the store and in the home-manager closure, but the per-user environment `/etc/profiles/per-user/$USER/share/` contains no `color-schemes/` directory.

## Workaround

Adding this to the system configuration resolves the warning and restores the configured palette for all Qt applications:

```nix
environment.pathsToLink = [ "/share/color-schemes" ];
```

## Suggested fix

Add

```nix
environment.pathsToLink = [ "/share/color-schemes" ];
```

to the `config` block of `nixos/modules/config/qt.nix` (guarded by `qt.enable`), since the module is what pulls in `plasma-integration` (via `platformPackages.kde`) and `breeze` (via `stylePackages.breeze`), and the directory is only needed when Qt platform integration is enabled. I have this change ready as a PR.

Alternatively the entry could be added to the global defaults in `nixos/modules/config/system-path.nix`, but that would link the directory on every NixOS installation including headless servers, whereas scoping it to `qt.enable` limits the change to configurations that actually use Qt platform theming.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.142.0 (6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1)
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200, x64, 8 logical processors

## Summary

When other processes keep the CPU busy (here: Windows Defender scans, an installer, the search indexer; 77-100% CPU), opening a notebook shows the notebook toolbar and a progress bar, but **no cell at all, code cells included, for 8 to 64 s** (in one series, twice not within 60 s). The VS Code window itself is idle meanwhile.

The back-layer webview's renderer process runs at Windows priority class **Idle** (plus EcoQoS) while the notebook warms up, because `_warmupWithMarkdownRenderer` sets the webview to `visibility: hidden` until the list is attached. The list is attached only after the webview has loaded the Markdown renderer and every renderer that extends it, so an Idle-priority process on a busy machine blocks the whole editor.

Why `visibility: hidden` does that: the webview is a cross-origin out-of-process iframe. In Blink, `LayoutEmbeddedContent::StyleDidChange` calls `Hide()` on the frame view when `visibility != visible`, the frame reports `FrameVisibility::kNotRendered`, `CrossProcessFrameConnector::OnVisibilityChanged` hides the child widget (`WasHidden`), the process has no visible client left, and `RenderProcessHostImpl::UpdateProcessPriority` sets `kBestEffort`, which on Windows is `IDLE_PRIORITY_CLASS` and EcoQoS (`base/process/process_win.cc`). A hidden cross-origin frame also gets its timers throttled to one wake-up per second. `opacity` is not part of that rule.

**A tested one-line fix:** hide the webview with `opacity: 0` instead of `visibility: hidden` during the warmup. In 6 alternating pairs the wait went from 9.8-62.7 s to 0-1.1 s (table below). Starting VS Code with `--disable-renderer-backgrounding` has nearly the same effect (it keeps the CPU priority, not the timer throttling).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Keep all CPU cores busy with other normal-priority processes.
2. `code --disable-extensions` and open a .ipynb with one Markdown cell and one code cell (no Jupyter extension needed).
3. The editor and toolbar appear; no cell is shown for seconds to a minute.
4. Repeat with `code --disable-extensions --disable-renderer-backgrounding`: cells show within about 1 s.

## The fix

In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/browser/notebookEditorWidget.ts`, `_warmupWithMarkdownRenderer`:

```diff
- this._webview.element.style.visibility = 'hidden';
+ this._webview.element.style.opacity = '0';
  await this._warmupViewportMarkdownCells(viewModel, viewState);
  ...
- this._webview.element.style.visibility = 'visible';
+ this._webview.element.style.opacity = '';
```

The webview stays invisible to the user, but Chromium no longer treats its frame as hidden, so its process keeps normal priority. Tested by patching the built 1.142.0 `workbench.desktop.main.js` (the two minified statements) and alternating original and patched builds, all extensions disabled, built-in .ipynb:

| Pair | Wait, original | Wait, patched | notebook-out/index.js load, original | patched |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 62.7 s | 0.0 s | 9.2 s | 17 ms |
| 2 | 56.6 s | 0.0 s | 11.1 s | 39 ms |
| 3 | 17.0 s | 1.1 s | 13 ms | 74 ms |
| 4 | 15.2 s | 0.0 s | 7.8 s | 15 ms |
| 5 | 48.6 s | 1.0 s | 13.2 s | 63 ms |
| 6 | 9.8 s | 1.1 s | 24 ms | 54 ms |

"Wait" = webview present to first cell row, measured in a fresh VS Code per open (Playwright).

With opacity 0 nothing can flash (the element is painted fully transparent), so the reason given in the comment for `visibility: hidden` still holds. The one difference is hit-testing: adding `pointer-events: none` for the same span keeps the transparent webview from taking clicks during the warmup.

## More measurements

- The same with `--disable-renderer-backgrounding` instead of the patch (all extensions disabled): 8.7-23.0 s vs 0-3.4 s; with an extension's notebook type: 8.0-63.9 s vs 0.0-1.6 s.
- Process priority, sampled every 2-5 s during control waits: window process **Normal** in every sample; webview process **Idle** (base priority 4) in 61 of 67 samples, Normal only in the sample where the cells appear. In a 64 s wait the webview process got 0.19 s of CPU in 27 s.
- The window's CPU profile during a slow open: main thread idle for 11 s of the wait.
- Direct reads of the same 185 KB file from another process at the same moment: 54-98 ms (so not disk or antivirus).
- In one slow open, after the Markdown renderer finished loading, the webview stalled another 13 s before requesting the extending renderers: no I/O in that gap, just no CPU.

## Where in the code

- `notebookEditorWidget.ts` `_warmupWithMarkdownRenderer`: hides the webview, awaits `_resolveWebview()` and `_warmupViewportMarkdownCells()` (`initializeMarkup` -> `initializedMarkup`), and only then calls `this._list.attachViewModel(viewModel)`.
- `webviewPreloads.ts` `Renderer._load`: imports and activates the Markdown renderer, then awaits every renderer that `extends` it.
- No timeout on `_resolveWebview` or `initializeMarkup`; only the webview service worker's 30 s `resolveTimeout` per request.

Other options, if opacity is not wanted: attach the list (at least code cells) without waiting for the Markdown renderers, or give the warmup a timeout.

The same symptom ("opening a notebook sometimes takes 5-20 s or never settles") was also seen on macOS CI runners (GitHub Actions). On a day with little slowness there, 3 runners with and without the flag gave 2 opens over 5 s without it and none with it: consistent, but not conclusive for macOS.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.142.0 (commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1, 2026-10-15), built-in Copilot Chat 0.70.0
- Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Model `claude-sonnet-5.5`, custom agent, agent mode
- Request options logged by the agent debug log:
  `{"thinking":{"type":"adaptive","display":"summarized"},"output_config":{"effort":"high"},"stream":true}`
- `chat.agent.thinking.collapsedTools` = `off` and `always`, and `chat.experimental.persistentProgress` removed: no difference

## Summary

When Sonnet 5.5 writes more than a sentence or two before a tool call, the text never arrives as a `text` block. The chat shows a collapsed thinking item with a generated title, then the tool call. The agent's next step often refers to the text ("as shown above") although the user never saw it.

This matches Anthropic's documented behavior, so it looks like a client gap rather than a model fault. Anthropic's docs describe that on Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5/5.1 and Mythos 5.1 a progress note between tool calls comes back as its own `thinking` block directly before the `tool_use`. With `display: "summarized"`, the docs say it is returned as a summary that is not distinguishable from reasoning. The docs recommend `display: "updates"` (beta header `thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18`) or, on Sonnet 5.5, `thinking: {type: "between_tools"}`, and rendering those blocks as visible text. They also say the full note is sent back to the model on the next request, which is why the model believes the user read it.

- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#progress-updates
- https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-sonnet-5-5#user-facing-progress-updates

## Where this happens in the Copilot Chat code

Source is public (MIT) in `microsoft/vscode`, `extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/messagesApi.ts`. The built-in 0.70.0 bundle contains the same logic.

- `createMessagesRequestBody` hardcodes the thinking config for adaptive-thinking models:
  `thinkingConfig = { type: 'adaptive', display: 'summarized' }` (the declared type only allows `display?: 'summarized'`).
- A search of the 0.70.0 bundle finds no occurrence of `between_tools`, `display: "updates"` or the `thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18` beta header.
- `AnthropicMessagesProcessor.push` treats every `thinking` content block alike: `thinking_delta` is forwarded as a `thinking` delta, and only `text_delta` becomes response text. A progress-update block therefore ends up as a thinking item, and the summary is all the client ever receives.

## Evidence from a controlled run

Same session and agent, 12 consecutive rounds. Each round the model wrote some text and then called `list_dir` / `read_file` (read-only), all after the first tool result. "Delivered" means the logged model response contains a `text` part.

| Round | Text written before the tool call | Delivered as `text` | Thinking summary block in response | Output tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | intro, 2 short sentences | no | yes | 1054 |
| T2 | 2 short sentences (162 chars) | yes | none | 136 |
| T3 | 5-sentence paragraph | no | yes | 278 |
| T4 | table + 1 sentence | no | yes | 204 |
| T5 | fenced code block + 2 sentences | no | yes | 201 |
| T6 | bullet list | no | yes | 215 |
| T7 | one short remark (72 chars) | yes | none | 106 |
| T8 | long numbered summary | no | yes | 509 |
| T9 | 3 short sentences | no | yes | 153 |
| T10 | 4 sentences | no | yes | 215 |
| T11 | one sentence (171 chars) | yes | none | 143 |
| T12 | table recap | no | yes | 918 |

Result: 3 of 12 delivered, all three one or two short sentences. The 9 that were not delivered were longer, or contained a table, list or code block (T9 is three short sentences). Every undelivered round has a thinking summary that paraphrases the lost text; every delivered round has none. Lengths of undelivered text are not recorded by the log, so they are not listed.

Working round (T2), `agent_response` for the model call, paths redacted:

```json
[{"role":"assistant","parts":[
  {"type":"text","content":"**[T2]** two sentences after a tool result. The skills folder holds four skills, all with an `fw-` prefix. Next I'll look at the agents folder to compare naming. "},
  {"type":"tool_call","id":"toolu_01CPaW...","name":"list_dir","arguments":"{\"path\": \"<repo>\\\\.github\\\\agents\"}"}
]}]
```

Failing round (T4), same session, same request options. The table and sentence I wrote do not appear anywhere in the response. Only a one-sentence summary reached the client, in a separate `reasoning` field:

```json
response:  [{"role":"assistant","parts":[
  {"type":"tool_call","id":"toolu_01Lo5j...","name":"list_dir","arguments":"{\"path\": \"<repo>\\\\.github\\\\prompts\"}"}
]}]
reasoning: "I've tallied entries so far: skills (4, all `fw-` prefixed), agents (5, mixed prefixes), and instructions (13, with 2 subfolders). Next I'll check the prompts folder."
```

The next request's history for that assistant message has only the same `reasoning` and `tool_call` parts and no text part.

In the chat UI the T4 text is not visible; only a thinking item with a generated title is shown, followed by the tool call.

## Impact

- Findings, plans and questions written before a tool call or a question widget are not shown, so the user answers without the context.
- Neither the user nor the model notices, because the model holds the full note. Instructions to "write it as chat text first" do not help for the same reason.

## Related reports (not verified by me)

- microsoft/vscode#314988: "Subagent's text messages not shown in chat" (closed; text before a question widget not visible)
- anthropics/claude-code#97504: "Messages meant for the user are sometimes emitted as hidden thinking before a tool call" (Opus 5.5, VS Code extension and CLI)
- anthropics/claude-code#96288: instructed verbatim relay is never emitted as text when a tool call follows (Opus 5.5)
- anthropics/claude-code#95764: prose between tool calls returned as summarized narration thinking blocks (Opus 5)
- can1357/oh-my-pi#14978: same on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 in another client

## Suggested fix

1. Request `display: "updates"` (with the beta header) or, for Sonnet 5.5, `thinking: {type: "between_tools"}`, and render non-empty progress-update `thinking` blocks as normal visible chat text (a distinct style is fine).
2. Alternatively, provide a message-sending tool that the model can use for exact user-facing text such as a table, snippet or question.

Both avoid depending on prompt instructions that other agent instructions may override.

## What I did not verify

- The server-side classification of the lost text as a progress update. The logs show that no `text` part arrives and that a summary appears in its place, which matches the documented behavior.
- Whether `display: "updates"` fixes it in Copilot Chat. I have not tested a modified build.
- The rate in other setups. Results above are one agent, one session, 12 rounds.

## Problem

When reviewing AI-generated code in VS Code, I often find several issues in non-contiguous code ranges, sometimes across multiple files.

Currently, my workflow is to add each selection as chat context and then manually write a numbered list explaining which question or suggestion belongs to which file and line range. Multiple attachments and multiple comments do not provide a clear, explicit one-to-one association. This creates unnecessary bookkeeping and makes feedback easy to misinterpret.

Asking through inline chat separately for each issue also interrupts the review and causes multiple agent interactions before I have finished collecting my feedback.

## Proposed workflow

1. Select a code range in the regular editor.
2. Use a context-menu action such as **Add Review Feedback to Chat**.
3. Enter a question or suggestion in an inline comment box bound to that selection.
4. Stage the comment in the current chat draft **without sending a request to the agent**.
5. Repeat for other non-contiguous ranges or files.
6. Review, edit, remove, or navigate to the staged comments from the chat draft.
7. Explicitly submit all comments as one request when ready, so the agent can address them together.

Each staged item should retain its file, code range, relevant code snapshot, and associated feedback. If the code changes before submission, the UI should flag stale anchors rather than silently associating feedback with different lines.

## Example

During one review, I might select:

- A test comment and ask whether it accurately describes the assertions.
- A different test case and suggest moving shared setup into a fixture.
- A function in another file and ask why an edge case is not handled.

I want to collect these locally while reading, then send them together. I should not have to copy line numbers or manually map numbered questions to separate context attachments.

## Relationship to existing functionality

The [review documentation](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/review-code-edits) describes inline feedback and **Submit Feedback** in the Agents window **Changes** view. This request is to make that style of workflow available directly from the **regular editor and the current chat draft**, including newly generated files, without requiring a pull request or switching to a separate review interface.

This is not just an **Add Selection to Chat** or **Ask in Inline Chat** action: the important combination is **selection-bound feedback + staging multiple comments + explicit batch submission**.

## Expected behavior

- Adding a comment should not start agent execution; only explicit submission should do so.
- Support multiple non-contiguous ranges and multiple files in one request.
- Keep each comment explicitly associated with its code context.
- Let the user request **explanations only** or **code changes** for the collected feedback; a question should not automatically imply permission to edit.

## Summary

Installing an agent plugin from a marketplace makes a full `git clone` of the source repository, even when the plugin lives in a small subdirectory and is pinned to a tag. For large monorepos this makes installs very slow, and on corporate networks (VPN / TLS-inspecting proxies) the long transfer often gets reset, so the install fails.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.142.0 (`6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1`)
- macOS 26.7.1 arm64, Git 2.56.0
- `chat.plugins.enabled: true`, private GitHub marketplace

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add a marketplace whose `marketplace.json` has an entry pointing at a large repository (~400 MB) with a sub-path and a tag:

   ```json
   {
     "name": "example-plugin",
     "source": {
       "source": "github",
       "repo": "<org>/<large-monorepo>",
       "path": ".github/plugin/example-plugin",
       "ref": "example-plugin-v1.0.0",
       "sha": "<40-char commit sha>"
     }
   }
   ```

2. Install the plugin from Agent Customizations, or via `vscode://chat-plugin/install?source=...&plugin=example-plugin`.

## Actual

VS Code runs:

```text
git clone --branch example-plugin-v1.0.0 -- https://github.com/<org>/<large-monorepo>.git <agent-plugins-dir>/...
```

This downloads the whole history of every branch reachable from the tag. On a good connection the install works but takes several minutes. On a corporate network it often fails:

```text
error: RPC failed; curl 56 Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
error: 1652 bytes of body are still expected
fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet
fatal: early EOF
fatal: fetch-pack: invalid index-pack output
```

Running the same clone by hand with `--depth 1` finishes quickly and works on the same network.

## Expected

Plugin installs should fetch only what they need. Two options, from simplest:

- Add `--depth 1` when cloning a branch or tag (`git clone --depth 1 --branch <ref> -- <url> <dir>`).
- For full-SHA pins (the path added in #339022), fetch just that commit: `git fetch --depth 1 origin <sha>`. GitHub allows this.

`--filter=blob:none` plus a sparse checkout of `path` would cut the transfer further for monorepos, but `--depth 1` alone already fixes the failures we see.

## Related

- #338581 / #339022 - SHA-pinned clones (same clone path, no depth limit)
- #317362 - git-subdir source: "the clone target remains the repository root"

## Summary

A restored Copilot CLI Agent Host session can continue ordinary conversation, but creating a new subsession or switching the session to an existing Git worktree fails with:

```text
Failed to activate restored private chats for copilotcli:/<session-id>: unavailable
```

The workspace switch never completes. Restarting VS Code did not resolve the failure.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.142.0
- Commit: 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1
- Build date: 2026-10-15T03:02:17Z
- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise, 10.0.26300, 64-bit
- Feature: Copilot CLI Agent Host sessions, restored subagent chats, workspace conversion
- Copilot Chat extension version: not captured; the failing stack is in VS Code's bundled Agent Host
- Selected model: not captured

## Steps to reproduce (observed sequence)

1. Restore an existing Copilot CLI Agent Host session with historical subagent conversations.
2. Ask it to create a new subsession. The `create_session` server tool fails with the error above.
3. Restart VS Code, restore the same session, and retry. The same failure occurs.
4. Ask the parent session to switch to an existing Git worktree containing pending edits.
5. The `set_workspace` tool initially reports that the workspace will be set after the turn ends, but the deferred workspace conversion fails with the same restored-private-chat error.

The exact session-state prerequisite has not been reduced to a minimal reproduction.

## Expected behavior

The session switches to the existing worktree, preserving its edits, and creating a new subsession succeeds.

If historical private-chat restoration cannot complete, provide an actionable recovery path and avoid unnecessarily blocking otherwise independent session operations.

## Actual behavior

- Restored private-chat admission fails at startup and on retry.
- `create_session` fails in the server tool handler.
- Workspace conversion fails after `set_workspace` has accepted the request.
- The parent session remains associated with its previous working directory.
- Pending edits in the destination worktree remain on disk; no Git move failure was observed.

## Sanitized diagnostics

The following entries are from the same session on 2026-10-20, local time (UTC+08:00). Identifiers and machine-specific paths are redacted.

```text
    [Copilot:<sdk-session-id>] Failed in server tool handler: tool=create_session

```

The session history confirms that `set_workspace` initially returned a deferred-success message, followed by a host-generated notification that workspace setup had failed and the requested task must not run.

## Investigation notes (not a confirmed root cause)

In the installed bundled Agent Host implementation, `_registerRestoredSubagentSummaries()` attempts chat catalog migration when the default chat is not normalized, the session catalog is enabled, and restored subagent chats exist.

It throws this error if migration returns no result or a status other than `applied`, `replayed`, or `alreadyNormalized`. The literal `unavailable` is also the fallback when the result/status is absent; it is not, by itself, evidence of a network outage.

`_migrateChatCatalog()` has early-return paths, including a `requiresLegacyChatCatalog()` compatibility check. Please investigate whether the restored-chat admission caller and catalog migration eligibility checks can disagree for restored/legacy sessions. The available logs do not establish which early-return path was taken.

Related, but not the same symptom: #332423 concerns restored historical subagent chats blocking subsequent parent turns. This report concerns catalog admission blocking `create_session` and workspace conversion; it does not establish a missing child transcript.

## Suggested regression coverage

- Restore a legacy session with historical subagent chats and exercise both `create_session` and conversion to an existing worktree.
- Cover migration being skipped because legacy catalog compatibility is required.
- Verify that optional historical-chat restoration does not unnecessarily prevent workspace conversion or unrelated session creation.
- Verify that failures preserve destination edits and retain consistent session/workspace metadata.

### Description

## Summary

On a machine with org-managed Copilot settings, opening an existing local (panel) chat triggers the automatic Move to Copilot. The new Copilot agent host session is created but never opened: the client subscribes with a `copilotcli:` URI, the provider refuses it, and about 30 seconds later the agent host disposes the session as empty. The original local chat is archived anyway. The user loses access to the chat (the session file is still on disk), and nothing replaces it.

Unarchiving doesn't help. Opening the chat again re-runs the move, which archives it again and creates another empty session that is also discarded.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.140.0 (stable), commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1, built 2026-10-15
- Windows client, remote WSL (Ubuntu) workspace
- Copilot agent host enabled, with the `copilotcli` provider
- Org-managed settings include a `permissions.*` key (`permissions.model`), which makes local panel chats read-only and turns on the automatic move (`autoMigrateLocalSession`)
- Affected chats are older local panel chats with long histories (the one I looked at is 131 MB in `workspaceStorage/<id>/chatSessions/`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have a local panel chat with history from before the agent host change.
2. With the managed settings above in effect, open that chat from the Sessions view.
3. Wait about 30 seconds, then look at the Sessions list.
4. Unarchive the chat and open it again.

## Expected

The history is moved into a Copilot agent host session that is saved and shown in the Sessions list. The local chat is archived only after the move has succeeded. If the move fails, the local chat stays as it was and an error is shown.

## Actual

- The local chat is archived (`archived: true` in `agentSessions.state.cache`).
- No new session appears in the Sessions list.
- After unarchiving, opening the chat archives it again within seconds and creates another empty session.
- No error is shown to the user.

## Log evidence

Agent host log (`agenthost.log`, remote), one attempt:

    13:09:37.291 [Copilot] Chat created; its backing stays deferred until the first send: ahp-session:/479f41a8-…
    13:09:38.040 [Copilot] Adoption declined for 479f41a8-…: marker=missing, provenance=unknown, cached=false
    13:09:38.076 [ProtocolServer] Request 'subscribe' id=3165 failed Provider copilotcli is not ready to open copilotcli:/479f41a8-…; it may still be starting, so try again shortly
    13:10:43.796 [AgentService] GC: disposing empty unsubscribed session ahp-session:/479f41a8-…

The session is created as `ahp-session:/<id>`, but the client subscribes to `copilotcli:/<id>`. Nothing ever subscribes to the real session, so it is collected as empty and the moved history is never saved.

The same happened four times in one day: `849835c8`, `23c70a5d`, `479f41a8` and `2fc36fa4` were all created and then removed with "GC: disposing empty unsubscribed session".

Renderer log at the same time:

    [error] Error: [UriError]: If a URI contains an authority component, then the path component must either be empty or begin with a slash ("/") character
        at Object.fromAgentHost (...)
    [error] Error: TreeError [AgentSessionsView] Data tree node not found: vscode-chat-session://local/<base64 session id>

## Impact

Several long-running chats can no longer be opened. The data is still on disk, but the only way back to it is to read the raw JSONL. Every attempt to open one makes it worse. There is no setting that lets a user turn the move off.

## Suggestions

- Archive the local chat only after the target session has been saved (or written to disk before the "first send").
- Subscribe to the session with the URI scheme it was created with.
- If the move fails, leave the local chat unarchived and show an error.

Full `agenthost.log` and `renderer.log` extracts can be provided on request.

# Feature Request: Time-Bound and Change-Aware Workspace Trust

## Summary

VS Code's Workspace Trust model currently focuses on whether a user trusts a folder or workspace. However, that trust can persist indefinitely, even when the underlying repository has changed significantly since the original trust decision.

I propose extending Workspace Trust with two complementary security mechanisms:

1. **Time-based trust revalidation** for workspaces that have not been opened for an extended period.
2. **Change-aware trust revalidation** when security-sensitive workspace configurations or executable files change.

The goal is to prevent a previously trusted repository from silently becoming an execution risk after a supply-chain compromise.

## The Problem

Consider the following scenario:

1. In January, a developer clones a legitimate GitHub repository, reviews it, and marks it as trusted in VS Code.
2. The developer does not open the repository again for several months.
3. In September, an attacker compromises the repository maintainer's GitHub account.
4. The attacker introduces malicious changes, including a `.vscode/tasks.json` containing a task configured with `"runOn": "folderOpen"`.
5. In October, the developer pulls the latest changes and opens the repository in VS Code.
6. VS Code remembers the previously granted Workspace Trust decision, even though the repository contents have materially changed.

If automatic tasks have been enabled, the malicious task could execute without the developer being prompted to reconsider the workspace's trust.

The original trust decision was legitimate. What changed was the code and configuration being trusted, not the folder itself.

This raises an important security question:

**Should a Workspace Trust decision remain indefinitely valid when the contents of that workspace have materially changed?**

## Real-World Supply-Chain Concerns

Recent supply-chain attacks, including the GhostAction campaign, demonstrate the importance of reviewing repository contents before allowing workspace-controlled execution.

Attackers can compromise legitimate repository maintainers and introduce malicious configurations or executable files into previously trustworthy repositories.

An additional warning sign is a repository that has been dormant for months or years and suddenly begins receiving commits.

This does not necessarily indicate a compromise. Legitimate projects can become active again. However, unexpected activity after prolonged inactivity is a worthwhile signal for additional scrutiny.

Reference:
https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/ghostaction-attackers-plant-credential.html

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Time-Based Workspace Trust Expiration

Introduce an optional or configurable Workspace Trust expiration policy.

For example:

- Revalidate trust after 30, 60, or 90 days of inactivity.
- Track when the workspace was last opened and when trust was last explicitly reviewed.
- If the workspace has changed since the previous trust review, require revalidation.
- Allow users and enterprise administrators to configure the expiration interval.

Simply reopening an unchanged workspace should not necessarily require a disruptive security prompt.

The intent is to introduce a periodic opportunity to reconsider trust, especially when a repository has changed during the period of inactivity.

### 2. Change-Aware Trust Revalidation

VS Code should detect security-sensitive changes to previously trusted workspaces.

Examples include:

- `.vscode/tasks.json`
- `.vscode/launch.json`
- `.vscode/settings.json`
- Workspace configuration files
- Newly introduced automatic execution tasks
- Changes to executable build or initialization scripts
- Changes affecting workspace-controlled command execution

Not all configuration changes are equally dangerous. The implementation should focus on changes that introduce or modify executable behavior rather than treating every file modification as a security event.

If sensitive changes are detected, VS Code should require revalidation before executing affected workspace-controlled functionality.

Importantly, this should apply both when opening a workspace and when changes occur while the workspace is already open.

### 3. Git Repository Awareness

For Git repositories, VS Code could use repository history as an additional signal.

Potential indicators include:

- A repository receiving new commits after a prolonged period of inactivity.
- Changes to security-sensitive configuration files.
- Unexpected changes to configured Git remotes.
- Newly introduced scripts or automatic execution configurations.
- Changes that occurred since the last Workspace Trust review.

The purpose would not be to classify repositories as malicious based solely on Git history.

Instead, these indicators could inform whether additional trust validation is warranted.

### 4. Prevent Execution Before Revalidation

One particularly important requirement is that revalidation must happen before potentially malicious workspace-controlled execution occurs.

For example, detecting a modified `.vscode/tasks.json` after a folder-open task has already executed would provide little security benefit.

The revalidation process should happen before affected tasks or other potentially dangerous workspace-controlled functionality can execute.

VS Code should also handle changes made while the workspace is open, including changes introduced by Git pull, checkout, merge, or external filesystem operations.

### 5. Provide Meaningful Context During Revalidation

Instead of simply asking users whether they trust a workspace again, VS Code should explain why the trust decision is being reconsidered.

Example:

**Workspace Trust Requires Review**

This workspace was last opened 127 days ago.

Security-sensitive changes have occurred since your previous trust review.

Changes detected:

- `.vscode/tasks.json` modified
- New automatic folder-open task introduced
- Four new commits since the last review
- Repository previously inactive for 11 months

Available actions:

- Review Changes
- Continue in Restricted Mode
- Trust Workspace After Review

The review should identify relevant changes and ideally provide a diff.

This would make the prompt actionable rather than another security warning that developers reflexively dismiss.

## Avoiding Security Prompt Fatigue

A major concern with this proposal is excessive security prompting.

If developers are asked to revalidate trust after every commit, the result would likely be approval fatigue.

The implementation should distinguish between:

- Ordinary source-code changes
- Changes to passive workspace configuration
- Changes to executable workspace configuration
- Changes introducing new automatic execution behavior

Revalidation should be risk-based and focused on meaningful changes.

Where practical, execution permissions could be suspended for affected functionality without unnecessarily disabling unrelated workspace features.

## Existing Protections

VS Code already provides Workspace Trust and Restricted Mode.

Additionally, the `task.allowAutomaticTasks` setting can disable automatic folder-open tasks.

These are valuable protections, but they address different concerns.

Workspace Trust establishes whether a workspace is trusted, while automatic task settings control one specific execution mechanism.

Neither provides comprehensive revalidation of a previously trusted workspace based on elapsed time or security-sensitive repository changes.

This proposal is intended to complement existing protections, not replace them.

## Suggested Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] VS Code can track the last explicit Workspace Trust review.
- [ ] Users can optionally configure a trust expiration period.
- [ ] Security-sensitive workspace configuration changes can trigger trust revalidation.
- [ ] Revalidation occurs before affected automatic execution.
- [ ] Relevant changes occurring during an active VS Code session are handled.
- [ ] Git history can optionally provide additional context.
- [ ] Users can review the changes that triggered revalidation.
- [ ] Users can continue in Restricted Mode without accepting new trust.
- [ ] Ordinary source-code changes do not cause unnecessary trust prompts.
- [ ] Parent-folder trust inheritance is considered so that trusting a parent directory does not silently bypass relevant security checks.
- [ ] Enterprise administrators can configure or enforce appropriate trust revalidation policies.

## Closing Thoughts

Workspace Trust is an important security boundary, but currently it is largely based on a persistent decision about a filesystem location.

In modern development, repository contents can change frequently, and a previously trustworthy repository can become compromised without the developer being aware.

Trusting a folder in January should not automatically imply that every executable configuration introduced into that folder in October deserves the same level of trust.

**Trust should account for both the passage of time and meaningful changes to the contents being trusted.**

I believe time-bound and change-aware Workspace Trust would provide a meaningful additional layer of protection against software supply-chain attacks while preserving the developer experience through targeted, risk-based revalidation.

### Proposal

Get rid of native OS dialogs (confirmation/message dialogs) and always use VS Code's custom (webview/DOM-based) dialogs instead.

Today this is partially controllable via the `window.dialogStyle` setting (`"native"` vs `"custom"`), but native remains the default/an option. Switching fully to custom dialogs would bring several benefits:

- They fit the VS Code theme more consistently than native OS dialogs.
- It's easier for agents to automate them (native OS dialogs are outside the DOM and can't be driven the same way as the rest of the UI).
- More control over how they steal focus — native dialogs can currently be very annoying about grabbing focus.

### Context

Raised in Slack by Henning Dieterichs ([@hediet](https://github.com/hediet)), with a screenshot showing a native dialog stealing focus. Lee Murray noted agreement, as long as it doesn't impact functionality.
